extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, applicants, representatives, and the public interested in DPMA examination procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Official guidelines of the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA) describing procedural and substantive criteria for filing, examining, communicating, granting/refusing, and publishing patent applications in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date, minimum requirements (sections 34, 35 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of filing is the date on which the documents referred to in section 34 (3) numbers 1 and 2 and, if they contain particulars to be regarded as a description, have been received by the DPMA (or designated patent information centre). The application must contain a request for the grant of a patent designating the invention clearly and concisely, the name of the applicant, and a description of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts (e.g., drawings or missing parts of the description) are filed subsequently after invitation or on applicant's initiative, the date of receipt of those parts constitutes the filing date; otherwise references to them are deemed not made. If documents are not in German, a German translation must be received within statutory periods (section 35a) otherwise application deemed withdrawn. If minimum requirements are fulfilled only successively the application is legally valid only after the last requirement is met; if not met the filing must be declared not a legally valid patent application after right to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination as to obvious deficiencies (section 42 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of examination is limited to requirements specified in section 42; if a legally valid application obviously does not comply with sections 34, 36, 37, 38 the examiner invites the applicant to remedy deficiencies within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious deficiencies that justify a communication include subject matter that obviously is not an invention, is not industrially applicable, or is excluded from grant under certain statutory provisions. If deficiencies are not rectified the application may be refused. If refusal would be based on circumstances not yet communicated, applicant must be given opportunity to comment first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of examining bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination as to obvious substantive deficiencies is carried out by patent examiners competent in the field; formal processing may be handled by officials of lower grades or comparable employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign technical substantive questions to competent examiners; formal handling (e.g., paperwork) follows delegation rules under sections cited (Wahrnehmungsverordnung, section 27(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (standard for objecting deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only deficiencies which are obvious may be objected to during examination under section 42; a deficiency is obvious if the examining section can recognize it as such without doubt and without further substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should not raise issues requiring full substantive investigation at this stage. The deficiency must be clearly evident from the submitted documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal deficiencies (enumerated types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal deficiencies that may be objected to include: incomplete request or deviation from power of attorney; doubts about whether patent is requested for applicant or company; in multiple applicants cases lacking authorised service person or missing signatures; missing parts of application (claims, description, drawings, abstract); incomplete or missing power of attorney; unclear/uncise title; missing or incomplete designation of inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deficiencies may be raised in the examination as to obvious deficiencies if they are evident from the documents. Specific remedies and time limits should be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of the inventor (section 37)
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation of the inventor must be submitted within 15 months from filing date or priority date (where applicable). If the applicant named himself sole inventor no separate document is needed unless inventor requests not to be mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If declaration is late due to justifiable exceptional circumstances a reasonable extension should be granted (section 37(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee (Patent Costs Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee pursuant to the Patent Costs Act is charged for the application; if fee is not paid, not paid in full or not paid in due time (within three months from filing) the application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure fee payment within statutory period; consequences of non-payment are strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of the Patent Ordinance (form/other requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application does not comply with form and other application requirements under the Patent Ordinance the examining section may refrain from objecting to these deficiencies until commencement of substantive examination (section 44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may restrict raised deficiencies to those that impede printing the first publication or prevent appropriate search. High standards of legibility and quality of documents are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiencies of the patent claims and description (grave deficiencies only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only grave deficiencies regarding contents and structure of patent claims and description are to be notified during examination as to obvious deficiencies; grave deficiencies are those that risk misleading the public at first publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should be made on the basis of the facts submitted and examiner's technical knowledge without using external material or full substantive searches; novelty and inventive step are not examined at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements pursuant to section 42(2) number 1 — Lack of an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter must be in one field of technology and must not obviously constitute a non-invention under section 1(3) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness of non-invention must be clear without further investigation; apply established case law where it answers the issue unequivocally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements pursuant to section 42(2) number 2 — Industrial application
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of industrial application must be recognisable without doubt and without further investigation when examining the application documents as to obvious deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purely therapeutic and diagnostic medical methods may be objected to if there is no doubt that no other use is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements pursuant to section 42(2) number 3 — Grounds for refusal (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for refusal under section 42(2) number 3 relate to exceptions to patentability (section 1a(1), section 2, section 2a(1)) — e.g., inventions whose commercial exploitation would be contrary to public policy or morality, human body, plant/animal varieties, essentially biological processes, methods of treatment by surgery or therapy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider Paris Convention limits: patent cannot be refused simply because sale/use is restricted by national legislation. Exception to patentability exists where substantial norms/principles of legal and moral order are affected; non-publication may be used for obviously problematic parts (ordre public/morality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity (obvious lack of unity assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination as to obvious deficiencies aims to prevent several obviously unrelated inventions being improperly combined in a single application; no obvious lack of unity where a technically useful unitary problem can be stated pre–state of the art and solution requires all parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity should be assessed on the documents; only obvious non-unity should be objected to at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of examination as to obvious deficiencies (timing and outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no obvious deficiencies found, note is made; if found, applicant invited to remedy within period. Examiner should ensure conclusive decision (refusal or dropping objection) is issued four months from filing at latest to enable corrected documents for first publication; if not possible uncorrected documents used for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant objects with sound reasons objections should be dropped; otherwise a further communication only in exceptional cases. Rejections must follow right to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference regarding division
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to the applicant about the possibility of division of an application; reference to section covering free division and divisional procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 2.3.3.5 for free division rules; examiners should inform applicants when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference regarding priority rights (substantive entitlement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive entitlement to claim priority (domestic or foreign) is not examined during the examination as to obvious deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions of entitlement can be examined later in substantive examination or opposition/invalidation proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting time limits in obvious-deficiencies stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit of four months for answering a communication may be reduced to two months if otherwise the examination cannot be completed before application is laid open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust time limits to ensure procedural milestones (e.g., lay open/publication) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents for the first publication (Offenlegungsschrift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents used for first publication are generally the originally filed documents; subsequently filed drawings/translations filed in due time are to be incorporated; unsolicited new documents filed by applicant are not used for first publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examination cannot be concluded before 18-month publication the uncorrected documents are used. If parts are obviously contrary to ordre public/morality, the DPMA may refrain from publishing problematic parts or, in exceptional cases, the entire application if publication would have no informative content after deletions. Make a note on the title page if published content differs from filing-date documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination (section 44 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for substantive examination is required under section 44; formalities and time limits apply for filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination does not start substantively until the request is made and handled formally; follow statutory deadlines and requirements when processing the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal handling of the request for examination and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules govern how requests for examination and responses to communications are to be formally handled and recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with filing formats, deadlines, and proper documentation of replies to communications (including time limits and service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of processing and prioritisation in substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining sections must follow internal order of processing, with provisions for handling workloads and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for accelerated processing may be considered under specified conditions; normal queueing applies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for accelerated processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request accelerated processing; criteria and handling rules apply to such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining section considers statutory and internal criteria when granting accelerated processing; follow listed procedures for handling requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of the invention (section 34(4) of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must disclose the invention sufficiently (clear and complete disclosure) so that a skilled person can carry it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sufficiency based on the application documents; use of drawings, examples, and possibly sequence listings or deposits (for biological material) to meet disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination as to patentability pursuant to sections 1 to 5 (basic requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination includes assessment under sections 1–5: patentable subject-matter, exclusions, state of the art, novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory tests and case law; separate assessment areas (e.g., subject-matter eligibility, novelty, inventive step).

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art (section 3 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the relevant prior art that defines novelty and inventive step comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and identify prior art documents (patent and non-patent) relevant to claimed subject matter; non-patent literature handling noted in public inspection section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (section 3 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether claimed subject-matter is new over the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty must be established via comparison to prior art; only claims lacking novelty are to be rejected on that ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (section 4 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether the claimed invention involves an inventive step relative to the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply relevant case law and technical assessment; for program-related inventions only technical features contributing to a solution of a specific technical problem count toward inventive step (see three-stage approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (section 5 of the Patent Act) in substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess that the invention is susceptible of industrial application as required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial applicability must be demonstrated; for medical methods consider whether other uses are possible when objecting under section 42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search within the examination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A search is conducted as part of substantive examination to identify prior art relevant to novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches should be adequate to support the examination; examiners may rely on available search tools and may cite search documents in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of documents / impermissible extension (section 38 of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to application documents are constrained by prohibition on adding subject-matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether amendments introduce new matter (impermissible extension); only permissible amendments that are supported by the original disclosure may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of unity of the application; division due to lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine unity of invention in substantive examination; if lack of unity is found a divisional or restriction may be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where lack of unity is established during substantive examination, division proceedings may be appropriate; follow statutory rules on division and unity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free division of the application (section 39(1) of the Patent Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may freely divide applications under statutory conditions (free division rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific provisions for timing and formality of divisional filings; inform applicants of options when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent claims and patent category (drafting and categorisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine claims for clarity, support by the description, proper categorisation (e.g., device, method), and allowable scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must meet statutory requirements; mark up for clarity and consistency with description; grave deficiencies only objected during obvious-deficiencies stage, but substantive claim defects addressed in substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications claiming a priority — domestic and foreign
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules govern how domestic and foreign priority claims are handled; formal and substantive issues arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities for claiming priority (timing, evidence) must be complied with; substantive entitlement is not examined at obvious-deficiencies stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other aspects of the substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch-all for additional substantive topics that may arise during examination (e.g., clarity, sufficiency, exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply case law and statutory guidance; take account of special circumstances and deviate from general principles where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications (section 45 of the Patent Act) — first and other communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The DPMA issues communications to applicants under section 45, including the first communication (often setting out search and substantive objections) and subsequent communications for further objections or clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First communication is treated specially (see paragraph 2.4.1). Other communications follow when necessary; time limits for replies and the possibility of reducing them (e.g., from 4 to 2 months) are set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting time limits (general substantive stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits apply for responding to communications and for procedural steps toward grant; the DPMA may set or reduce time limits to meet publication/grant schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicant is given reasonable time; where necessary reduce periods to meet statutory milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings and telephone conversations (section 46 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings (in-person or via audio/video) may be held; telephone calls and unscheduled contacts are governed by rules about calling and participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory provisions for hearings; allow attendance via image and sound transmission where provided for; document telephone communications and calls without invitation carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of the grant of the patent applied for — filing and editing of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for filing documents ready for grant and editing official documents prior to grant (e.g., finalising description, claims, drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure hand-over of corrected, printable documents; prepare the specification for publication and grant according to formatting, language, and content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions of the examining section (section 47) — decision to grant (section 49) and to refuse (section 48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination culminates in formal decisions to grant or to refuse the application according to sections 47–49 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must state reasons; refusal requires prior opportunity to comment if grounds not previously communicated; grant requires finalisation steps (fees, translations if needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of appeal and review against decisions of the examining section (procedural routes and time limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out appeal paths to the Federal Patent Court and review options; adhere to statutory times and requirements for filing appeals and requests for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures: biotechnological inventions — general aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications concerning biotechnological inventions have special requirements (e.g., deposit of biological material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed deposit requirements: date of deposit, information concerning depositary institution and material, duration of storage, furnishing of samples and undertakings, furnishing proof of deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of a deposit (biotech) — detailed items
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit must meet rules on date, depositary information, duration of storage, provision of samples, undertakings and proof to satisfy disclosure and enable reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deposit complies with standards and is documented in the application; missing or improper deposit affects sufficiency/industrial applicability and may be objected to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-related inventions (computer-implemented) — technicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess 'technicity' pursuant to section 1(1) — whether claimed subject-matter qualifies as an invention (technical character) rather than being excluded (mathematical method, program, business method, presentation of information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the three-stage approach derived from Bundesgerichtshof case law: (1) technicity check, (2) whether a concrete technical problem is solved by technical means (exceptions), (3) novelty/inventive step of the solution (sections 3 and 4). Consider examples where program-controlled settings of device parameters achieve technical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to patentability for program-related inventions (section 1(3),(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether claimed subject-matter is excluded as mathematical method, method for doing business, or presentation of information, and whether claimed instructions solve a specific technical problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-technical instructions that merely collect/store/analyse data are relevant only to the extent they influence a technical solution. Visual/presentation features that account for human perception may contribute to solving a technical problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage examination approach for program-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: First: examine technicity. Second: examine whether a concrete technical problem is solved by technical means (exceptions). Third: assess novelty and inventive step of the technical solution under sections 3 and 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply stage tests sequentially. For inventive step only technical features that contribute to solving the technical problem are considered; non-technical instructions are considered only insofar as they influence the technical solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further aspects regarding program-related inventions (drafting and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be drafted in German technical language but may contain customary foreign-language technical terms. Description may include data flow charts, program flow charts and short program excerpts where conducive to intelligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow short code excerpts in customary programming language if they aid understanding. Diagrams showing time sequences and operational steps may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions relating to artificial intelligence (AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-related inventions may concern AI-specific foundations (hardware, algorithms, models) or applications using AI. No established case law yet; program-related approach and three-stage examination are generally transferred to AI inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply explanations for program-related inventions by analogy; consider whether AI features produce a technical effect/solve a technical problem and whether technical features contribute to inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing the public — file inspection and publication rules (section 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: DPMA grants any person inspection of files (including online inspection) for published applications, except where precluded by statute, overriding data protection interests, or parts obviously contrary to ordre public/morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-patent literature is not shown for copyright reasons unless expressly requested under section 31(1) sentence 2. File inspection is available electronically via DPMAregister if case file activated. Keep restrictions limited to problematic parts where possible.
